correctness.rationale: For a norming pair (x,x*) and every y∈B_X, each z with x*(z)=1 satisfies ||z-y||≥1-x*(y); equality is attained exactly by z=y+(1-x*(y))x. Infimizing gives eta_X(epsilon,(x,x*))=upsilon_X(epsilon,(x,x*)) with no compactness assumption. Under symmetric Birkhoff orthogonality w=y-x*(y)x is orthogonal to x in Birkhoff sense, so ||w||≤||y||≤1; then ||x-y||≤2-x*(y) establishes eta_X(epsilon)≥max(0,epsilon-1). In the hexagonal norm N(s,t)=max(|s|,|t|,|s-t|), quarter-turn of the polar hexagon establishes Birkhoff symmetry; y=(1,epsilon) for epsilon≤1 and y=(2-epsilon,1) for epsilon≥1 meet the lower envelope identically. Inspected full source verify.py and independently evaluated the exact rational unit-ball witnesses; the 401-point grid is supplementary, not the continuum proof. The claim is for real Banach spaces; boundary epsilon=0,1,2 is covered.
